quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Enhertu recommended for approval in the EU by CHMP as (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The EMA's CHMP recommended EU approval of AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu (trastuzumab deruxtecan) as monotherapy for the adjuvant treatment of adults with resected HER2-positive breast cancer who have residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant taxane-based and HER2-targeted treatment. The opinion is based on the DESTINY-Breast05 Phase III trial (1,635 patients), in which Enhertu reduced the risk of invasive disease recurrence or death by 53% versus T-DM1 (hazard ratio 0.47; 95% CI 0.34-0.66, p<0.0001); at three years 92.4% of Enhertu patients were alive and free of invasive disease versus 83.7% on T-DM1, with no new safety concerns. This indication is already approved in the US, Brazil, India and Canada. Enhertu was discovered by Daiichi Sankyo and is jointly developed and commercialised by AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo (collaboration since March 2019; Daiichi Sankyo keeps exclusive rights in Japan and is responsible for the manufacturing and supply of Enhertu and Datroway).
